claims.text: Introducing a thin Cr interlayer into HEA multilayers will shift creep from diffusion-mediated toward dislocation-mediated deformation.
Cr has moderate atomic diffusivity.
Cr has favorable lattice matching with the unspecified HEA multilayers.
A Cr interlayer can promote interface coherency in HEA multilayers.
Cr-induced interface coherency limits fast diffusion paths.
The Cr interlayer acts as a barrier that favors dislocation activity.
The initial HEA multilayers have incoherent or less-engineered interfaces.
The initial HEA multilayers exhibit predominantly diffusion-mediated creep at high temperatures.
A deposited thin Cr interlayer will form a coherent interface with the HEA multilayers.
The coherent Cr interlayer alters interfacial atomic structure and reduces effective diffusion paths.
The Cr interlayer enables dislocation interactions at the interfaces.
Moderate Cr self-diffusivity and lattice matching reduce atomic diffusion across the interface.
Reduced interfacial diffusion shifts the dominant deformation mechanism toward dislocation-mediated creep as strain accommodation progresses.
Cr-containing multilayers will have lower steady-state creep rates than otherwise identical multilayers without Cr interlayers.
Cr-containing multilayers will exhibit higher interfacial dislocation density or greater slip-system activation than controls.
The proposed effect will be most pronounced at temperatures and stresses where diffusion and dislocation mechanisms compete.
At sufficiently high or low temperatures, one creep mechanism may dominate regardless of interfacial modification.
Cr interlayer thickness critically controls the proposed effect.
An excessively thin Cr interlayer may be ineffective.
An excessively thick Cr interlayer may introduce additional deformation modes.
